c.tagline: China's hottest oasis — grapes, ruins, and the Flaming Mountains.

taxi.fareNote: City taxis are metered and Didi works in town, but the major sights are spread across the desert — most visitors hire a car with driver for the day.

emergency.note: 110 reaches police, 120 is for ambulance/medical and 119 is fire.

avoid.reason: Xinjiang — security checkpoints and surveillance; carry your passport; check advisories

hood_desc: The compact downtown hub of the oasis, with the covered bazaar, Turpan Museum, grape-trellised streets, hotels and restaurants; the walkable base most visitors stay in.
A lush vineyard gorge just north of town where grapes grow on shaded trellises and family homestays and guesthouses cluster; a cool, scenic retreat and a classic Turpan sight.
The area beside the Jiaohe (Yarkhoto) Ruins west of the city — a spectacular earthen ancient city on a river island; quiet and dramatic, dominated by the archaeological site.
The desert stretch east of town below the red Flaming Mountains, taking in the Gaochang Ruins, the Bezeklik Thousand Buddha Caves and the Astana Tombs; the sightseeing heartland, reached by car.
The southeastern edge of the oasis around the 18th-century Emin Minaret and its mosque, threaded with old Uyghur lanes and vineyards; traditional and local in feel.

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water, as is standard across China.

transit.hours: City buses run roughly 7:00 AM to 9:00 PM; taxis and Didi cover the rest, and most sights outside town need a hired car.
transit.note: Turpan is a small oasis city with local buses and taxis but no metro or in-city rail; the main sights are spread across the surrounding desert and are best reached by hired car or tour.
transit.pay: City bus fares are paid in cash or by mobile payment (Alipay/WeChat) on board (about 1-2 yuan); taxis are metered.

bus: Turpan Bus Station — coaches to Ürümqi (~2.5 h), Hami and Shanshan

car.idp: Foreign licences/IDP not valid in China — most visitors hire a car with driver

train: Turpan North Railway Station — Lanzhou–Xinjiang high-speed line, ~1 h to Ürümqi

tip.r: Tipping is not customary or expected in mainland China; there is no need to tip in restaurants or taxis.
